ethics_check.title: Ethics Approval Check
ethics_check.summary_text: All papers that appeared to involve live data collection contained an ethics approval statement.

table.text: Limited by federal law to investigational use.) and by the Institutional Review Boards at Mass General Brigham (protocol #2009P000505), Brown University (protocol #0809992560), the VA Providence Healthcare System (IRB-2011-009), and Emory University (protocol #00003070).

Using both standard performance assessments and conversational tasks, we show that iBCIs can achieve substantially improved brain-to-text error rates compared to previous BCIs in our participants with a chronic pontine stroke.

We then blueprint the data requirements to achieve high-performance brain-to-text in our participants, and we show that we can adjust for the effects of signal nonstationarities in new sessions by fine-tuning our brain-to-text decoder with as few as 22 new training sentences for T16 and 41 new training sentences for T22.
To compare performance across different vocabularies, participants were cued with sentences from either a 50-word vocabulary 9 or from the Switchboard corpus representing a large vocabulary 26.
table.formatted: To compare performance across different vocabularies, participants were cued with sentences from either a 50-word vocabulary <ref type="bibr" target="#b9">9</ref> or from the Switchboard corpus representing a large vocabulary <ref type="bibr" target="#b27">26</ref>.

table.text: During inter-trial periods, participants were instructed to rest.
This indicated the beginning of the delay period, during which time the participants were instructed to read but not yet attempt to say the sentence.
T16 and T22 gave informed consent prior to any experimental procedures.

ethics_check.report:
Based on the following text, we would expect an ethics approval statement, and it was present:

> Using both standard performance assessments and conversational tasks, we show that iBCIs can achieve substantially improved brain-to-text error rates compared to previous BCIs in our participants with a chronic pontine stroke.

> We then blueprint the data requirements to achieve high-performance brain-to-text in our participants, and we show that we can adjust for the effects of signal nonstationarities in new sessions by fine-tuning our brain-to-text decoder with as few as 22 new training sentences for T16 and 41 new training sentences for T22.

> To compare performance across different vocabularies, participants were cued with sentences from either a 50-word vocabulary 9 or from the Switchboard corpus representing a large vocabulary 26.

> During inter-trial periods, participants were instructed to rest.

> This indicated the beginning of the delay period, during which time the participants were instructed to read but not yet attempt to say the sentence.

> T16 and T22 gave informed consent prior to any experimental procedures.

Ethics approval statement:

> Limited by federal law to investigational use.) and by the Institutional Review Boards at Mass General Brigham (protocol #2009P000505), Brown University (protocol #0809992560), the VA Providence Healthcare System (IRB-2011-009), and Emory University (protocol #00003070).

power.title: Power Analysis Check
report:
::: {.callout-tip title="Learn More" collapse="true"}

Power analyses need to contain the following information to be interpretable: the type of power analysis, the statistical test, the software used, sample size, critical alpha criterion, power level, effect size, and an effect size metric. In addition, it is recommended to make sure the power analysis is reproducible (by sharing the code, or a screenshot, of the power analysis), and to provide good arguments for why the study was designed to detect an effect of this size.

For an a-priori power analysis, where the sample size is determined, reporting all information would look like:

> An a priori power analysis for an independent samples t-test, conducted using the pwr.t.test function from pwr (Champely, 2020), indicated that for a Cohen's d = 0.5, an alpha level of 0.05, and a desired power level of 80% required at least 64 participants in each group.

For a sensitivity power analysis, this sentence would look like:

> A sensitivity power analysis for an independent samples t-test, conducted using the pwr.t.test function from pwr (Champely, 2020), indicated that with 64 participants in each group, and an alpha level of 0.05, a desired power level of 80% was reached for an effect size of d = 0.5.

:::
